title: The Pettiford family band, the Bias brothers and Charlie Christian
summary: Albert turned down the Pettiford family band in order to keep his word to Troy Floyd; then they discuss Bias brothers and Charlie Christian's origin.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, Oscar Pettiford, that's the band I was supposed to go with when I went to Troy's band. Oh, you were going with the Pettiford? They wanted me. And I had Richard McCarthy from here and Lucian Johnson. And I told them what I was going to do, so I told Richard, I said, Richard, I can get you in this little band if you want to stay. He wanted to come back to New Orleans. So I talked to Pettiford and he only just wanted me in the band. And I told him, no, I had already told Troy that I was going to join him and I didn't want to go against my word. Which Pettiford was this? This was Oscar's mother, Oscar Pettiford. And his sister was the decisive one. I can't recall all her names right now, but it was a family band. The daddy played the drums, the mother played the piano. And Harry was Harry Pettiford, great tenor player. And then Oscar was the young one, the bass player, he was the young Pettiford.
Did you know the biases? Sure, all of them were there?
No, they're from Birmingham, aren't they? I thought they were from Muscogee too.
I thought they were from Birmingham. They may be, I know. I know that Don was around there or something. Don Bias? Yeah, there's so many Midwestern musicians.
Well, I always connected Don Bias with the brothers, Doug Bascom and his brother. They may have been, I don't know.
Now you have another one, Christian, the guitarist? Yeah, Charlie. Charlie Christian. Well now he was from Oklahoma City. A lot of people said Tulsa, where are any fields this from?
